request.system:
You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.

messages.content:
Bill number: HB1032

<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 1032

 By Dixie

 AN ACT to amend Chapter __ of the Public Acts of 2025
 (1st Ex. Sess. – SB 6002 / HB 6001); and
 Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 4; Title 5; Title
 6; Title 7; Title 8 and Title 49, relative to education.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) As used in this section, "immigration officer" means any state, local, or

 federal law enforcement officer who is seeking to enforce immigration law, including, but

 not limited to, United States immigration and customs enforcement officers and United

 States customs and border protection officers.

 (b) Notwithstanding title 4, chapter 42 and title 7, chapter 68, the director of

 schools for the LEA or the director of the public charter school shall immediately notify all

 students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school, parents of students enrolled in the

 LEA or public charter school, and all educators, employees, and contractors of the LEA

 or public charter school of the presence of an immigration officer on the grounds of a

 public school controlled by the LEA or on the grounds of the public charter school.

 (c) Notwithstanding §§ 4-42-102 and 7-68-102, this section and any policy

 adopted by a local board of education or public charter school governing body to

 effectuate this section is not a sanctuary policy and does not subject a member of the

 local board or governing body, director of schools, director of the public charter school,

 or any employee of the LEA or public charter school to any penalty prescribed in title 4,

 chapter 42 or title 7, chapter 68 for the adoption or enforcement of a sanctuary policy.

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

summary: This bill would add a new section to the part of Tennessee law that covers local school systems (LEAs) and public charter schools. It defines an "immigration officer" as any state, local, or federal law enforcement officer who is seeking to enforce immigration law. The definition includes, but is not limited to, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers and U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers. Under the bill, if an immigration officer is present on the grounds of a public school run by an LEA, or on the grounds of a public charter school, the director of schools or the director of the charter school would have to notify people right away. Those to be notified are all students enrolled in the LEA or charter school, their parents, and all educators, employees, and contractors. This duty would apply despite Title 4, chapter 42 and Title 7, chapter 68 of the Tennessee Code, which are the chapters referred to in the bill's sanctuary policy provisions. The bill also says that this notice requirement, and any policy a local school board or charter school governing body adopts to carry it out, is not a sanctuary policy. As a result, board or governing body members, school directors, and LEA or charter school employees would not face the penalties in those two chapters for adopting or enforcing a sanctuary policy. The bill would take effect as soon as it becomes law.
